messages:
jess_support: Customer hitting intermittent 502s on hosted API /v1/complete. Support ticket #12345. Gateway logs show repeated TLS handshake timeouts, looks regional-agnostic. Repro window ~2026-03-17T14:30Z.

jess_support: sample gateway line: `2026-03-17T14:31:09Z ERROR gw=hosted-1 conn=10.0.0.45 tls_handshake_timeout peer=198.51.100.23`

jess_support: customer sent a quick curl test — sometimes works, sometimes fails with 52/Connection reset: `curl -v --max-time 5 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete`

alex_oncall: thanks Jess — can you get a traceroute/tcpdump from the client side and the gateway side for a failing request? Also need client IP + whether requests are short/long-lived (streaming).

alex_oncall: quick repro suggestion: `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -msg` and `curl --http1.1 --no-keepalive -v ...` — if no-keepalive helps that points to stale pooled sockets.

maria_infra: noting we rolled a gateway config yesterday, keepalive backend pool = 90s. If customer NAT/firewall drops idle TCP earlier, we can hand out a stale FD and the next TLS handshake fails. Common in corp NATs with 60s idle.

maria_infra: short-term mitigations: lower gateway backend keepalive to 30s, enable TCP keepalive probes for backend connections, or set gateway to prefer `Connection: close` for customers under investigation. Kernel knobs we use for testing: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time=60` `net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_intvl=10` `net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_probes=5`

dan_runtime: also check ALPN/ECN/MSS corner cases — I've seen ECN-marked packets cause mid-stream resets on middleboxes. Can you `tcpdump -w out.pcap host 198.51.100.23 and port 443` and paste a small capture? netstat on gateway would show many ESTABLISHED sockets in the pool vs TIME_WAIT if pooling is sticky.

opsbot: deploybot: canary gateway config deploy completed 2026-03-17T14:00Z (keepalive=90s).

jess_support: customer says they're behind a corporate NAT with aggressive 60s idle kill. Their streaming clients often pause for >2min between chunks, so idle-to-reuse is common. They tested `curl --http2 --no-keepalive` and that succeeded consistently.

jess_support: customer asks for immediate workaround — recommended they try toggling client keepalive or switch to short-lived connections. Can we also flip gateway keepalive down to 30s for hosted edge while we triage?

alex_oncall: I'm opening INC-2026-789 and assigning to infra + runtime. Immediate action: 1) lower gateway backend keepalive to 30s in canary, monitor 502 rate for affected customer; 2) enable TCP keepalive probes on backend pool; 3) add a short-term rule to prefer `Connection: close` for their tenant. Long-term: detect and proactively evict stale pooled fds and add heuristics for streaming workloads behind NATs.

maria_infra: agree. I'll push keepalive change to canary now and watch telemetry. If we see error drop for that customer, roll to full.

dan_runtime: I'll add a small probe on the runtime side to validate TLS handshake after reusing a socket and evict on handshake failure. Also will check ECN flags in recent tcpdumps.

jess_support: thanks — I'll update the customer with the mitigation plan and request tcpdump/traceroute. Will report back here with their pcap if they can provide it. :thumbsup:

eve_cust: thx team, we can pull a pcap but need guidance on exact capture cmd.

alex_oncall: give them: `sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/cust.pcap host <client_ip> and port 443` and `traceroute -n api.redwood.ai`. Also ask them to capture at the time they see a 502.

jess_support: noted. I'll send commands and update ticket. Keeping thread open until post-mitigation verification.
